Drogon: CMake Release (CMake's default -O3 -DNDEBUG) in the drogonframework/drogon:latest image, without -march=native, with jemalloc LD_PRELOADed.
corrections.claimed_speedup: baseline-4096: 4,381,919 req/s vs libreactorng 4,377,377 (+0.1%, derived from page data, a tie), h2o 3,641,609 (1.20x, derived), nginx 3,284,513 (1.33x, derived) and Drogon 2,022,710 (2.17x, derived). On limited-conn-4096 (connections close after 10 requests) libxev's 2,672,662 is behind libreactorng's 2,685,717 (-0.5%, derived) and level with h2o (2,651,569) and nginx (2,626,297). latency-1m/10k/500k-8cpu are fixed-rate profiles scored on CPU per request, not throughput.
corrections.workload: HttpArena baseline profile: mixed GET/POST /baseline11 requests with query parsing (sum of query integers plus the body), 4096 keep-alive connections, pipeline depth 1, 5 s runs. Server on 32 cores / 64 threads of a Threadripper PRO 3995WX, gcannon load over loopback. The HTTP/1.1 server is written in Zig on libxev's io_uring backend, with one forked worker per CPU, SO_REUSEPORT and TCP_NODELAY, and parses requests with picohttpparser (C).
corrections.caveats: The libxev README says it will not post benchmark results and claims only that you 'shouldn't notice a slowdown' against other event loops, so the figure here is an HttpArena application, not a library claim. Request parsing is done by picohttpparser (C, compiled at -O3), so the Zig code is the event loop, the glue and the arithmetic. Against the best C entry (libreactorng, also io_uring and SO_REUSEPORT per CPU) the result is a tie on baseline (+0.1%), and libreactorng is 0.5% ahead on limited-conn. The margins over h2o, nginx and Drogon reflect io_uring against epoll engines and minimal handlers against full servers (nginx runs a custom C handler module), not Zig codegen. The libxev server does no routing (every path gets the sum response) while libreactorng dispatches on the path, a small saving for the Zig side. The results JSON files are undated and are rerun by the suite's maintainers; competitor rows come from sibling JSON files in the same directory. HttpArena is a smaller suite (about 128 GitHub stars) than TechEmpower.
corrections.why_faster: Not a language win. libxev's io_uring backend with one forked worker per CPU and SO_REUSEPORT (frameworks/libxev/meta.json and src/main.zig) is the same design as the C entry libreactorng, which it only ties. The gains over h2o, nginx and Drogon come from io_uring against epoll and from a minimal handler against full servers.

tier_reason: The numbers are on performance_summary.md and in the README, but the benchmark is degenerate and gives no valid language measurement. The Rust binary is unoptimised (plain rustc, no -O), and each server is a single-threaded, syscall-bound accept/read/write/close loop. Each server got one 10 s wrk run with no hardware or compiler versions stated, and the byte-for-byte equivalent C and C++ servers differ by 23%. That is the degenerate-benchmark precedent (ThreadPool, hop) for D.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Makefile: gcc -O2 blade_core.c, g++ -O2 blade_core.cpp, 'rustc blade_core.rs' with no -O or opt-level (an unoptimised debug build), and 'zig build-exe blade_core.zig' (Debug by default). No compiler versions. The C/C++ side is not -O3, and the optimisation levels are not matched.
corrections.caveats: Not a valid language comparison. The Rust build has no optimisation flag while C and C++ use -O2. All four servers are the same single-threaded blocking loop (accept, one read, write a fixed 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... OK' response, close), so the time goes to kernel accept/close and the wrk client, not to language codegen. The C and C++ servers are functionally identical yet differ by 23% (32,976 vs 40,715 req/s), which shows the run-to-run noise exceeds the claimed Rust margin. There is one 10 s run per server and no repetitions, and CPU, kernel and compiler versions are not stated. Minor asymmetries: the Rust server binds 127.0.0.1 while C and C++ bind INADDR_ANY (wrk connects to 127.0.0.1 in every case); Rust uses write_all and unwrap() (a reset would abort the server) where C and C++ do a single write; C reads 1023 bytes and C++ 1024. The listen backlog is 128 in C, C++ and Rust std alike. The Zig row (80,700 req/s) came with 701k write errors. The repo has 0 stars and a single commit (2025-07-12).
corrections.why_faster: Nothing attributable to Rust: an unoptimised Rust build beating -O2 C on a syscall-bound accept/close loop, with identical C and C++ code 23% apart, means the ordering is measurement noise from a single wrk run each.

notes: Downgraded C to D under the degenerate-benchmark precedent. It is kept rather than rejected because the numbers are real runs, not fabricated or a no-op. Shortcomings to record: Rust built without -O while C/C++ use -O2 (not -O3); the syscall-bound accept/close loop shows no language effect; identical C and C++ servers 23% apart; single 10 s run; no hardware or compiler versions; 0 stars, 1 commit, stale.
